newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 97 GDP, industrial output seen flat or down.
newsitem.headline: Russia 97 GDP, industrial output seen flat or down.

text.p: New figures underpinning the Russian government's plan to cut spending to cope with revenue shortfalls show that both gross domestic product (GDP) and industrial output could fall by up to two percent this year.

The figures, presented to the State Duma lower house of parliament by First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, said both GDP and output would be flat or down two percent this year. Forecasts underpinning the original budget envisaged GDP growth of up to two percent.
The government said GDP fell five percent in 1996, while industrial output was also five percent lower. Previously Russia had said GDP had fallen six percent in 1996.

The government said output in large and medium-sized enterprises was likely to fall three percent this year. But, taking into account likely growth in smaller firms and in the hard-to-measure shadow economy, overall output would be flat to two percent below 1996 levels.
The government also said it expected investment to fall by up to five percent in 1997 from 1996. Early figures had envisaged growth of up to two percent.

Ministers have been saying for weeks that the long-awaited industrial turnaround will come next year rather than this year. Chubais said last week that living standards would start to improve next year for the first time since the start of painful reforms designed to create a market economy.
